As <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.9">Ec 11:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.10">10</reference> showed what youths are to shun, so this verse shows what they are to follow.<div eID="gen12781" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12782" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Creator--</hi>"Remember" that thou art not thine own, but God's property; for He has created thee (<reference osisRef="Ps.100.3">Psa 100:3</reference>). Therefore serve Him with thy "all" (<reference osisRef="Mark.12.30">Mr 12:30</reference>), and with thy best days, not with the dregs of them (<reference osisRef="Prov.8.17">Pr 8:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.22.6">22:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.3.4">Jr 3:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.3.27">La 3:27</reference>). The Hebrew is "Creators," plural, implying the plurality of persons, as in <reference osisRef="Gen.1.26">Ge 1:26</reference>; so Hebrew, "Makers" (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.5">Is 54:5</reference>).<div eID="gen12782" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12783" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">while ... not--</hi>that is, before that (<reference osisRef="Prov.8.26">Pr 8:26</reference>) the evil days come; namely, calamity and old age, when one can no longer serve God, as in youth (<reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.8">8</reference>).<div eID="gen12783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12784" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no pleasure--</hi>of a sensual kind (<reference osisRef="2Sam.19.35">2Sa 19:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.90.10">Psa 90:10</reference>). Pleasure in God continues to the godly old (<reference osisRef="Isa.46.4">Is 46:4</reference>). <div eID="gen12784" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 12 Ec 12:1-14 . 1. As Ec 11:9 , 10 showed what youths are to shun, so this verse shows what they are to follow. Creator-- "Remember" that thou art not thine own, but God's property; for He has created thee ( Psa 100:3 ). Therefore serve Him with thy "all" ( Mr 12:30 ), and with thy best days, not with the dregs of them ( Pr 8:17 ; 22:6 ; Jr 3:4 ; La 3:27 ). The Hebrew is "Creators," plural, implying the plurality of persons, as in Ge 1:26 ; so Hebrew, "Makers" ( Is 54:5 ). while ... not-- that is, before that ( Pr 8:26 ) the evil days come; namely, calamity and old age, when one can no longer serve God, as in youth ( Ec 11:2 , 8 ). no pleasure-- of a sensual kind ( 2Sa 19:35 ; Psa 90:10 ). Pleasure in God continues to the godly old ( Is 46:4 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8184"/><div sID="gen12805" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8184"/>6. A double image to represent death, as in <reference osisRef="Eccl.12.1-Eccl.12.5">Ec 12:1-5</reference>, old age: (1) A lamp of frail material, but gilded over, often in the East hung from roofs by a cord of silk and silver interwoven; as the lamp is dashed down and broken, when the cord breaks, so man at death; the golden bowl of the lamp answers to the skull, which, from the vital preciousness of its contents, may be called "golden"; "the silver cord" is the spinal marrow, which is white and precious as silver, and is attached to the brain. (2) A fountain, from which water is drawn by a pitcher let down by a rope wound round a wheel; as, when the pitcher and wheel are broken, water can no more be drawn, so life ceases when the vital energies are gone. The "fountain" may mean the right ventricle of the heart; the "cistern," the left; the pitcher, the veins; the wheel, the aorta, or great artery [Smith]. The circulation of the blood, whether known or not to Solomon, seems to be implied in the language put by the Holy Ghost into his mouth. This gloomy picture of old age applies to those who have not "remembered their Creator in youth." They have none of the consolations of God, which they might have obtained in youth; it is now too late to seek them. A good old age is a blessing to the godly (<reference osisRef="Gen.15.15">Ge 15:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.5.26">Job 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.16.31">Pr 16:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.20.29">20:29</reference>). <div eID="gen12805" type="x-p"/>

The grand inference of the whole book.<div eID="gen12818" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12819" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Fear God--</hi>The antidote to following creature idols, and "vanities," whether self-righteousness (<reference osisRef="Eccl.7.16">Ec 7:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.7.18">18</reference>), or wicked oppression and other evils (<reference osisRef="Eccl.8.12">Ec 8:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.8.13">13</reference>), or mad mirth (<reference osisRef="Eccl.2.2">Ec 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.7.2-2Cor.7.5">7:2-5</reference>), or self-mortifying avarice (<reference osisRef="Eccl.8.13">Ec 8:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.8.17">17</reference>), or youth spent without God (<reference osisRef="Eccl.11.9">Ec 11:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.12.1">12:1</reference>).<div eID="gen12819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12820" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">this is the whole duty of man--</hi>literally, "this is the whole man," the full ideal of man, as originally contemplated, realized wholly by Jesus Christ alone; and, through Him, by saints now in part, hereafter perfectly (<reference osisRef="1John.3.22-1John.3.24">1Jo 3:22-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.14">Re 22:14</reference>). <div eID="gen12820" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 13. The grand inference of the whole book. Fear God-- The antidote to following creature idols, and "vanities," whether self-righteousness ( Ec 7:16 , 18 ), or wicked oppression and other evils ( Ec 8:12 , 13 ), or mad mirth ( Ec 2:2 ; 7:2-5 ), or self-mortifying avarice ( Ec 8:13 , 17 ), or youth spent without God ( Ec 11:9 ; 12:1 ). this is the whole duty of man-- literally, "this is the whole man," the full ideal of man, as originally contemplated, realized wholly by Jesus Christ alone; and, through Him, by saints now in part, hereafter perfectly ( 1Jo 3:22-24 ; Re 22:14 ).
